svg.title: JEJ Notional Machine — the program's lifecycle
svg.desc: JEJ Notional Machine, organized around the program's lifecycle as two acts. Act 1 SETUP is syntactic (source, tokens, ast) and derives the static environment: the initial scope tree with every binding reserved in the temporal dead zone. Then RUN: the derived environment enters the world and comes alive. Act 2 RUNTIME is evaluation inside the realm; the realm (ECMA intrinsics and host bindings) is the world the program runs in and the top of the scope chain (block to module to realm). Evaluation has three interlinked cells: code (what the code says), nm (the semantics: the dynamic environment, scope and prototype chains, values, coercion), and host (the I/O buckets: dev console and user dialogs). The arrows between cells are the observable trace events resolve, coerce, emit, and return.
svg.text: JEJ Notional Machine — the program's lifecycle
Two acts, like a debugger: ① SETUP — parse, then derive the static environment (paused) · ② RUNTIME — evaluation inside the realm (stepping)

g.text: One program, four audiences read it:
the machine (parses & evaluates) · the reader (names & structure)
agents collaborate across all four — see the package README.

svg.text: — syntactic; the realm isn't engaged yet · parse the text, then derive the static environment

grammar — what the code says (the control panel)
no functions, classes, arrays, var, try/catch
invalid grammar · e.g. break outside a loop · let redeclaration (detected statically, before anything runs)
declarations come to be — before anything runs
the scope tree is derived; every let/const is
block scopes are derived here too, entered later
tdz = uninitialized — reading it throws ReferenceError

▶ RUN — the derived environment enters the world and comes alive

svg.text: — evaluation, inside the realm · the debugger's "stepping" view

g.text: 🌍 REALM — the world the program runs in · host-installed before any code · the top of the scope chain
a program wakes into a full JavaScript realm; JEJ teaches this slice of it — "what is mine to use?"
ECMA intrinsics — the language's, always present (SetDefaultGlobalBindings §9.3.4)
easter egg — admitted, untaught (not in reference.md)
no globalThis · `new RegExp()` is refused (Date is the only `new`)
callable values are marked ƒ · object-registers (Math, String, Number, Date, RegExp) are boxes of methods with a prototype
Host bindings — the browser's, not the language's
"this is JavaScript" vs "this is your browser"
alert / confirm / prompt PAUSE evaluation until the user responds
▲ the scope chain's top is the realm — name resolution walks block → module → realm
evaluation — the program runs · each arrow between cells is an observable trace event
what the code says — the live line
which value came from which syntax
the code text is the control panel;
the machine itself is next door (nm)
environment · DYNAMIC — the SAME scopes from setup, now live
status: tdz → initialized → dead · const: never updates → TypeError
a block pushes an env on entry (only if it has let/const),
pops on exit (reason: normal / break / continue / error / limit)
walk outward until the name is found; fall off the top → ReferenceError
same shape as the scope chain — walk a chain to find a name · protoChainWalk
values — string · number · bigint · boolean · null · undefined
coercion — implicit, observable only in the trace
postfix x++ returns OLD · prefix ++x returns NEW · ??= skips PutValue when non-nullish
where the program's effects reach humans

Runtime errors (no try/catch — all terminal): ReferenceError (TDZ access · unresolvable name) · TypeError (call non-callable · prop on null/undefined · const reassign · bigint+number) · RangeError (out of range · JEJ `limit`)
See notional-machine.md for the prose model & ECMA-262 spec correspondence.
